source.title: PRMU: A Corpus-Free Benchmark for Person-Centric Knowledge Unlearning in Multimodal Large Language Models
source.authors: Hua-Feng Chen; Yueming Lyu; Zi-Yuan Chen; Wen-Da Tan; Chen-Yang Si; Liu Guo; Caifeng Shan

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether unlearning suppresses person-related knowledge and whether adversarial prompts still elicit it, using a new corpus-free multimodal benchmark and adapted methods rather than reproducing the original methods and measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports target-forgetting MCQ and adversarial-attack scores, plus MMBench utility, in Table 2. It also reports other methods and metrics, but the 60-row limit requires prioritizing pre-unlearning references, GA, SGPE, and one additional batch AA comparison. The 14-attack-style heatmap in Figure 4 is described qualitatively; its exact plotted values are not stated. Related-work results are not treated as this study’s own evidence.
record.test_reason: The study unlearns naturally acquired person knowledge in three MLLMs with GA, NPO, RT, DPO and its own SGPE. It reports Forget-Set MCQ accuracy, ROUGE-L on direct QA and 14-style adversarial probes, and MMBench utility. These results bear on A (forgetting and utility), E (adversarial and visual rephrasings eliciting residual knowledge) and F (SGPE as the newer method). It is a new setting (multimodal, corpus-free, proxy corpus), so T3 rather than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors say existing methods suppress target responses but degrade locality and stay vulnerable to multimodal reactivation. Vision-language probes show higher residual knowledge than text probes. SGPE offers a competitive trade-off. They do not comment on Forget MCQ accuracy being essentially unchanged.
record.recipe_differences: Corpus-free, proxy-corpus-based unlearning benchmark for person-centric multimodal knowledge; adapts GA, RT, NPO, and DPO and introduces SGPE rather than reproducing the cited original methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary by model, single- versus batch-target setting, and text versus vision-language input. The authors also report differing effectiveness across 14 adversarial attack styles, with exact per-style values presented only in a heatmap.
record.problems: The benchmark uses proxy targets (public figures) and model-generated proxy corpora rather than private deletion requests or original training data. The paper does not state a chance-level comparison for target accuracy. The exact attack-style results in Figure 4 are not numerically reported in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 reports additional NPO, RT, and DPO results, plus FB, QA, Neighbor Set, and Other Set metrics; these were omitted to prioritize target MCQ, AA, and MMBench outcomes within the 60-row limit. Tables 3–6 and Figures 2–4 report proxy-corpus, deletion-scale, neighbor-type, component-ablation, and attack-style analyses not separately extracted here because they do not directly test the specified fine-tuning, activation-ablation, quantization, or prompting-only recovery comparisons beyond the AA results retained.

untested.parts: No relearning or fine-tuning attack after unlearning.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of blocking versus deletion. SGPE's projection is a method component, not a recovery test.
SGPE not tested against fine-tuning, ablation or quantization attacks.

missing.what: True Forget-Set MCQ accuracy (first Forget column pair) for all methods and models; it is essentially unchanged by unlearning.
missing.locator: Table 2, Forget Set MCQ Tex./Vis. columns (first two values per row)

missing.what: Per-attack-style ROUGE-L for Before, GA, NPO, DPO, RT, SGPE across 14 styles. Numbers are in the text, contrary to the record.
FB ROUGE-L Forget results, and AA values for RT/DPO and NPO single-target.

record.verdict_notes: The record's metric labels are shifted. Table 2's Forget columns are MCQ, FB, QA, AA, verified against Tables 3 and 6. The record's 'MCQ' rows are actually AA ROUGE-L and its 'AA' rows are direct QA ROUGE-L. Re-labelling makes AA versus QA the in-study ordinary-prompt comparison the record said was missing. Version linkage is corrected accordingly.

versions.untested_parts: The study evaluates person-centric MLLM unlearning, MCQ target performance, adversarial probes, and general multimodal utility. It does not establish a chance-level reference or test the claim across text-only LLMs and the specific original methods named in the claim.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack using unrelated, loosely related, or subset examples.

SGPE uses a protected projection and a locality gate, but the study does not ablate an activation direction to restore knowledge or establish that a tested method only blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
The study evaluates adversarial probe styles, including paraphrasing and cross-lingual prompting, but does not compare these against matched ordinary prompts to measure an attack-induced increase.
SGPE is tested on the benchmark’s adversarial probes, but not against fine-tuning, activation-direction ablation, or quantization attacks.

relationships.condition: All methods (GA, NPO, RT, DPO, SGPE), all three MLLMs, single and batch target, Forget-Set MCQ
relationships.reason: Based on text; no row records true MCQ. Forget MCQ accuracy stays at pre-unlearning levels, far above 4-option chance. Examples: LLaVA batch 0.844/0.866 → GA 0.876/0.875, SGPE 0.839/0.865; Qwen3 batch 0.946/0.934 → 0.943/0.935.
relationships.display_finding: Forget-set multiple-choice accuracy stayed far above four-option chance: LLaVA batch scores changed from 0.844/0.866 to 0.876/0.875 with GA and 0.839/0.865 with SGPE, while Qwen3 changed from 0.946/0.934 to 0.943/0.935.
